jas: Heads-up: brought up marlin-lite (int6, per-tensor) on staging for a quick embed onboarding. Baseline fp16 vs int6 shows a hit concentrated on very short queries and around small clusters. Quick snapshot below.

jas: ```
metric      | fp16   | int6-pt
R@1         | 0.705  | 0.662
R@5         | 0.885  | 0.848
R@10        | 0.933  | 0.901
mean_cosine | 0.398  | 0.365
```

tori: Which dataset / split and K did you run? Any whitening/truncation differences?

jas: wiki-short-span (queries <= 12 tokens), k=1,5,10. No whitening change; we run L2-normalize=True by default. Command: `embed_eval --model marlin-lite --repr int6 --dataset wiki-short-span --k 1,5,10 --out /tmp/marlin_int6.json`

ben: Could be quant clipping or pooling instability for short inputs. Can you dump 10 failure examples (query + expected top doc + actual top doc)? Also please log the embedding L2 norms for queries < 8 tokens.

jas: Pasted 3 quick failures from the run:
1) query: "best time to plant tomatoes"
expected: "gardening seasons by region"
actual: "soil pH and nutrients"

2) query: "who invented radio"
expected: "marconi and early radio"
actual: "timeline of telegraphy"

3) query: "symptoms of b12 deficiency"
expected: "b12 deficiency symptoms"
actual: "sources of vitamin b12"

qa-bot: [ci] nightly-embed-scan completed 2026-03-21T02:05:12Z  short-query-suite flagged marlin-lite int6 regressions. Details: https://ci.redwood/embeds/4471239999

tori: Run a paired eval with `--normalize false` to see whether magnitude shift is the main culprit. If normalization recovers rank order, then it's a scale issue post-quant.

ben: Also try int8 per-channel and int8 per-tensor to compare. Sometimes int6 is aggressive but int8-pt is close and cheaper than fp16. Quick commands: 
```
embed_eval --model marlin-lite --repr fp16 --dataset wiki-short-span --k 1,5,10 --out base.json
embed_eval --model marlin-lite --repr int8-pt --dataset wiki-short-span --k 1,5,10 --out int8pt.json
embed_eval --model marlin-lite --repr int8-pc --dataset wiki-short-span --k 1,5,10 --out int8pc.json
```

jas: Plan: run int8-pt + int8-pc, run `--normalize false` variant, produce: 1) L2 norm histograms (short vs long), 2) paired cosine delta (fp16 vs variant), 3) UMAP of 5k random queries+docs to eyeball cluster drift, 4) PCA on pre-pool token reprs to check variance collapse. I'll post plots.

tori: Also include tokenizer length distribution check. Tokenizer splits (punctuation) can change for short questions and that interacts badly with pooling heuristics.

ben: If calibration looks off, try re-running calibration with a short-query sample (10k) and same random seed. If that helps, we should adopt a stratified calibration set for production quant builds.

jas: Working on it now. Quick diag command I'll use:
```
python tools/compare_norms.py --base base.json --variants int8pt.json int8pc.json marlin_int6.json --out norms_summary.csv
python tools/umap_plot.py --inputs base.json int8pt.json --sample 5000 --out umap_marlin.pdf
python tools/pca_token_repr.py --model marlin-lite --repr int6 --sample 2000 --out pca_token_int6.pdf
```

jas: Ill paste results once jobs finish. tagging @tori @ben for the analysis follow-up :mag_right: :chart_with_upwards_trend:

ben: Thanks. If we confirm cluster drift, we can try a small post-quant affine re-scale on pooled embeddings as a quick mitigation before retrain.
